findings.text: Generic pack and unpack front ends accept a packed buffer with its length, a host object, a descriptor array and quirks. They first run compile time descriptor validation and buffer size validation, then select a width specific helper according to whether descriptors are byte or halfword entries, forwarding buffer, length, object, array, element count and quirks.

Descriptor validation supports arrays sized one through fifty inclusive through a chained compile time selector with one dedicated checker per size, and larger arrays fail the build with a request to extend the generator.

Work item carries queuing linkage, a back pointer to shared parallel state, a designated callback processor, a sequence number, an integer info field, and two operation hooks for parallel and serial phases.
Ordered queue object pairs a list head with a spin lock member held in the same object.
The queue object embeds its own spinlock, indicating list mutation and traversal are intended to be serialized by that lock rather than an external one.
Serial queue groups a private ordered list, a work item for deferred execution, and a back pointer to shared parallel state.
CPU assignment groups two masks distinguishing processors used for parallel work from processors used for callbacks.

Generation state links back to its shell, holds per processor reorder lists and per processor serial queues, a reference count, current sequence and processed counts, a CPU identifier, and embedded CPU assignment.
Shell links to its owning instance, holds a read copy update protected current generation pointer plus a prior generation pointer for teardown, and linkage for membership in an instance list.

Multithreaded job describes a range routine taking start, end and argument, an opaque argument, a start offset, total size, alignment, minimum chunk size, maximum thread count, and a NUMA awareness switch.
Instance groups hotplug linkage, separate parallel and serial workqueues, a shell list, active CPU assignment, a validation mask, a kernel object, a mutex, and a flag byte.
Instance embeds a mutex alongside its queues, shell list and masks, indicating instance reconfiguration and state transitions are intended to be serialized by that mutex.
CPU role selectors use distinct low bits, serial being one and parallel being two.
Instance lifecycle flags occupy distinct low bits, init one, reset two and invalid four.

In this configuration initialization is empty and multithreaded execution degrades to a single synchronous call of the range routine over the full start to start plus size interval with the supplied argument.
Headers use standard multiple inclusion guards.
Zone field width follows a shift chosen among zero to three in four build alternatives, and width equals the selected shift.
Section field is either sized from physical address capacity minus section size or disabled to zero, with width tracking the chosen shift or zero respectively.
Node field width either mirrors node shift or is zero, with a marker constant indicating the node is absent from page flags.
Sanitizer tag width is eight, four or zero across three build alternatives.

Last CPU and process tracking combines an eight bit process component with a CPU component sized from CPU count bits, summed into a combined shift, with width either tracking that shift or zero, plus a marker for absence and masks derived from each shift.

Reference history width is capped by remaining space after accounting for base flags and all other field widths, non flag bit count sums section, node, zone, CPU process, tag and generation widths, and unused count is word size minus flags plus non flag bits.
Flag mask covers exactly the low bits up to the count of distinct page flags.

Core flags cover locking, writeback, recency, validity, dirtiness, LRU membership, compound headness, waiter presence and activity among other lifecycle and ownership roles, with head fixed in position six and waiters in position seven sharing a byte with lock, plus conditional mlock, poison, young, idle and extra architecture flags and a terminal count.

Several logical flags reuse physical bits, including read ahead sharing reclaim, swap cache and checked and Xen pinned and foreign and remapped and self hosted map sharing the first owner bit, anonymous exclusive and mapped to disk sharing the second owner bit, save pinned sharing dirty, movable isolated sharing reclaim and movable sharing uptodate, reported sharing uptodate, cache sharing the second private bit, and folio only poison aggregate, large remappable and partially mapped reusing active, working set and reclaim in the first tail word with a ban on low and any context bits.

Tail detection uses the low bit of compound info, head resolution either derives a stored head address or masks a tail address when power of two page size optimization is enabled, setting stores either an address with low bit set or a shift derived mask with low bit set, and clearing zeroes the field.
Predicates report tail from compound info low bit and compound from head bit or tail bit, poison is recognized by an all ones flag word, and poison initialization is empty in this configuration.
Folio flag accessor selects the nth page word after asserting the base is not a tail and that indexed access beyond zero only applies to a head.

Page policy wrappers always check for poison, with variants accepting any page, resolving to head, forbidding tails, forbidding compound pages, or selecting the second page of a head, enforcing misuse through debug assertions.
Folio policy selectors map any, head, no tail and no compound to word zero and second page handling to word one, with matching head and second page index constants.

Flag helper generators provide test, set, clear, non atomic set and clear, and test and set or clear operations for both folio and page levels, combined into full and atomic only bundles, plus false and no operation variants used when a feature is disabled.

Using a poisoned page, operating on a tail where head is required, operating on compound where plain page is required, placing folio only flags in forbidden bits, or supplying a descriptor array whose footprint exceeds the packed buffer can corrupt state or fail the build; callers must validate poison state, headness and buffer capacity before flag or packing operations.
